correctness.rationale: Conditional implicit midpoint is exactly a Gaussian AR(1) kernel with coefficient \(r(u)=(1-u)/(1+u)\) and innovation standard deviation \(\sqrt{1-r(u)^2}\). Every conditional kernel preserves \(N(0,1)\); synchronous coupling contracts by \(q_2<1\). The first two Hermite polynomial regression identities give exact stationary lag powers and integrated autocorrelations. Strict convexity of \(r\) proves the linear penalty. For quadratic mode \(f=r^2\), the explicit contact identity \(f(u)-\ell_B(u)=(B-u)(Bu-B-2)^2/((B+1)^3(1+u)^2)\) and \(f(u)=8(2-u)/(1+u)^4\) yield the full lower convex envelope; Jensen plus equality conditions prove the exact phase boundary and uniqueness. Symbolic identities and 9,952 exact rational two-atom cases passed in the attached verifier; finite checks are not the all-laws proof.

value.rationale: Random-time-step schemes naturally impose an arithmetic mean and bounded step range. The first two Hermite modes are canonical scalar Gaussian sampling observables. Their exact opposite variance responses give a meaningful constraint on sampler design: linear variance is always harmed by randomization, while a sharp cap-dependent region permits a unique two-point law that improves quadratic variance. The closed-form cap threshold and rational example provide a reproducible benchmark, even though this scalar harmonic model does not estimate an unknown Gaussian moment.
